summary.intent: Fix DatePicker's `_unlocal_date` so the displayed value stops lagging one day behind the user's manual selection for users in UTC+ (ahead-of-UTC) time zones, per issue #9129, and add the widget's first integration test file.
summary.issue_fit: Met — the reported round-trip bug (select a day, see the day before) is fixed and reproduced as resolved for UTC+2 and UTC+13 test zones; the same code change introduces a new, previously-untested regression for behind-UTC time zones (see the must-fix finding).
summary.coverage: Both changed files fully reviewed against the merge-base diff: the `_unlocal_date` change and its two changed call sites in `bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts`, and the new `tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py`. Traced the property round trip through `bokeh/models/widgets/inputs.py`, `bokeh/core/property/datetime.py`, and `bokeh/util/serialization.py` to establish that `value`/`min_date`/`max_date` always arrive client-side as UTC-midnight epoch-ms timestamps. The project's own Selenium integration suite could not run (no browser/build in this sandbox); a focused Node.js reproduction of the exact `_unlocal_date` bodies from both the merge-base and the head commit, run under several `TZ` values, substituted for it and was independently repeated and confirmed by a fresh-context verifier.
check_details: The repository's own Selenium integration suite (tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py) could not be run: no browser or project build is available in this sandbox; its assertions were instead inspected by trace and found not to exercise either the fixed bug or the new regression, since both concern how `_unlocal_date` maps a timestamp to a calendar day under different browser time zones, which the suite never varies.

Reviewer-executed: `node` reproduction of `_unlocal_date`'s merge-base and head bodies against a UTC-midnight input and a re-parsed local-midnight input, under TZ=Europe/Paris, TZ=America/New_York, TZ=Pacific/Auckland, and TZ=UTC — confirms the fix for ahead-of-UTC zones and the new regression for behind-UTC zones; independently reproduced by the verifier across additional zones (Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Kiritimati) with the same result.

findings.title: Guard `_unlocal_date`'s new offset shift to reparsed local-midnight inputs
findings.trigger: A `DatePicker`'s `min_date`, `max_date`, or an unselected initial `value` is rendered in a browser whose local time zone lags UTC (a positive `getTimezoneOffset()`, e.g. `TZ=America/New_York`); those properties always arrive from Python as UTC-midnight epoch-ms timestamps.
findings.impact: The new `getTimezoneOffset`/`setTime` lines subtract that offset unconditionally, shifting the UTC-midnight timestamp into the previous UTC day before `toISOString()` reads the calendar date, so the widget renders `min_date`, `max_date`, and the initial date one day earlier than the caller set; the merge-base code read the same input correctly.
findings.change: Only apply the offset correction when `date` is not already at UTC midnight, e.g. guard the two new lines behind `if (date.getUTCHours() || date.getUTCMinutes() || date.getUTCSeconds())`, so wire-format UTC-midnight values stay untouched while the reparsed local-midnight round trip from `_on_select` still gets corrected.

observations.fact: `_unlocal_date` mutates its `date` parameter in place via `setTime`, which is only safe because both call sites pass a freshly constructed `Date` that nothing else reads afterward.

requirements.evidence: bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:79-87 (head): the added offset correction makes the post-selection round trip read the correct calendar day. Reproduced in Node with the exact merge-base and head `_unlocal_date` bodies: under TZ=Europe/Paris and TZ=Pacific/Auckland (ahead-of-UTC zones, matching the reporters' France/UK locations), the merge-base round-trip path returned the day before the selection while the head version returns the selected day.
